answer: Each agent may submit claims, but only claims backed by a scarce, nontransferable stake can earn rewards: the protocol locks that stake before a task and slashes it when independent checks show fabricated work. One operator can mint many identities, yet each must lock capital and risk losing it, so splitting into sybils multiplies the cost without multiplying honest value. A harbor operator might label a test batch umber; if false claims ripple through the batch, the bonded loss makes the attack expensive.
